points.title: It is no exaggeration to say that

items.sentence: The festivities *do not end* until the participants have celebrated for nine days and journeyed over 300 kilometers in central Taiwan.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Adverbial clause (until...)

items.sentence: Undoubtedly, the Mazu pilgrimage *is* a can't-miss event for visitors to Taiwan.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vl + C + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: The pilgrimage, which honors the sea goddess Mazu, *sets out* from Dajia's Zhenlan Temple around her birthday, the twenty-third day of the third month on Taiwan's lunar calendar.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (which...) + Vi (Phrasal verb) + Prepositional phrases + Appositive

items.sentence: The exact date and time, which vary from year to year, *are determined* earlier.
items.pattern: Compound S + Relative clause (which...) + Passive verb phrase + Adverb

items.sentence: During the Lantern Festival, temple authorities *cast* two half-moon-shaped wooden blocks to decide the actual schedule.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: At the chosen time, some 200,000 pilgrims *set out* from Zhenlan Temple on foot and *visit* more than 100 temples over the course of nine days.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Compound verb phrase + O + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: They *are accompanied* every step of the way by a statue of Mazu, which is carried in a sedan chair.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Adverbial phrase + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: Although the pilgrims' strength may wane during the long journey, never do their passion and dedication *fade*.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Although...) + Inverted adverb + Auxiliary + Compound S + Vi

items.sentence: Apart from being a chance for people to show their devotion to the goddess, this annual festival *is* a spectacular and heart-warming event.
items.pattern: Prepositional gerund phrase + S + Vl + C

items.sentence: The gathering in front of Zhenlan Temple before the pilgrimage begins *is* a scene like no other.
items.pattern: S + Adverbial clause (before...) + Vl + C

items.sentence: Throngs of people *fill* the streets, while the explosive sounds of drums, horns, fireworks, and firecrackers pierce the air.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Adverbial clause (while...)

items.sentence: When the statue of Mazu finally emerges from the temple in her sedan chair, the crowd *surrounds* her, excited to send her off on her long journey.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + S + Vt + O + Participial phrase

items.sentence: Along the route, millions of people also *join in* the celebration and *come out* to receive her blessing.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Compound verb phrase + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Some even *kneel* or *lie* face down on the pavement to allow the sedan chair to pass over them, which symbolizes their hope for good luck.
items.pattern: S + Compound verb phrase + Infinitival phrase + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: In the meantime, locals *show* their hospitality by enthusiastically offering free food, washing facilities, and accommodations to passing pilgrims.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vt + O + Prepositional gerund phrase

items.sentence: Rarely can such generosity *be seen* during a religious event.
items.pattern: Inverted adverb + Modal + S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: It *reflects* not only the locals' dedication to Mazu but also the warmth and humanity that are characteristic of the Taiwanese people.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Correlative compound O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Over the years, the Mazu pilgrimage *has transformed* into more than just a religious ritual, and every year it *attracts* all manner of people-young and old, foreign and Taiwanese.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vl + C + and + Adverbial phrase + S + Vt + O

items.sentence: Thus, the Mazu pilgrimage *has been designated* as one of Taiwan's important national folk customs.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Passive verb phrase + C

items.sentence: For those who are looking to experience Taiwan's cultural heritage, participating in the Mazu pilgrimage *is* essential!
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase with Relative clause (who...) + Gerund phrase (S) + Vl + C

text_genre.raw_text:
Passage Structure Analysis (5W1H Descriptive Pattern)
Introduction & What / How Big (Para 1): Introduces the Mazu pilgrimage as the world's largest/wildest birthday party (5+ million people, 9 days, 300+ km) and establishes its importance as a must-see event in Taiwan.
When / Who / How (Para 2):
When: Lunar March 23rd period, determined during Lantern Festival via wooden blocks.
Who & How: 200,000 pilgrims on foot carrying Mazu's statue in a sedan chair across 100+ temples.
Where / Why / What Happens (Para 3):
Where & What: Starting from Dajia Zhenlan Temple; streets packed with drums, fireworks, and crowds.
Why & Cultural Spirit: Pilgrims seek blessings (crawling under the sedan chair), while locals show hospitality (free food, lodging) reflecting Taiwanese warmth and generosity.
Conclusion & Significance (Para 4): Summarizes the pilgrimage as a designated national folk custom and an essential cultural heritage experience.
